_notes: Feature-gate config, read client-side by every page. Missing file, missing key,
or an expired subscription (see below) are all treated identically: every
feature behaves as if it were 'true'. This file lives in config/ specifically
because that directory is NOT copied by the mirror-signal.yml / mirror-intel.yml
workflows -- a mirrored deployment (The-Signal, Intel) simply won't have this
file at all and will run fully open unless a config/site.json is added there
directly, independent of this one. That's what makes this the basis for a real
per-deployment subscription-tier system later: each deployed copy of the site
can carry its own config/site.json with its own flags.
Each value under "features" is normally a plain boolean. A feature that needs
an extra switch (currently only "podcast", for spotlight.html's in-page audio
player vs. linking out to the source) is an object instead: {"enabled": bool,
...extra switches}. Both shapes are handled by every page's loader.
"ads" is a simple on/off for the sponsored slides in the spotlight/intel
digest carousels -- disabling it just removes them, no locked/teaser state.
Every other feature, when disabled, still shows in the digest carousels but
capped to a single locked/watermarked teaser item instead of its normal count,
and the corresponding standalone page (where one exists) redirects to
index.html with a 'Subscribe for Access' message -- see README's Feature
gating section for the full behavior.
"subscription" is shaped after JWT claims (sub/iss/iat/exp) on purpose, so a
future version of this loader can swap a fetched JSON file for a verified JWT
without changing the shape features are read in. None of it is enforced yet
beyond exp (and only if it's actually set -- it defaults to null, i.e. never
expires): alg is deliberately "none" (the real, defined JWT value for
'unsecured, do not trust this for access control') until real signature
verification exists.
